claims.statement: Article 50 transparency obligations apply from 2 August 2026 to specified providers and deployers, with official guidance covering marking, detection and disclosure questions.
The legal scope is risk- and use-case-specific, so a publish-gate product must classify context rather than label every asset indiscriminately.

contrary_evidence: Model providers and major content platforms can add native provenance, open standards may commoditise marking, and not all AI-assisted content is in scope.

risks: False scope classification can cause over-disclosure or noncompliance.
Robust marks can be stripped or degrade content.

structure.control_point: CMS or asset-library publish and export action
structure.critical_dependency: generator provenance signals plus legally sufficient marking and disclosure policy

thesis: Provide a CMS and digital-asset-management SDK that detects in-scope synthetic or manipulated content, applies required disclosure/marking policy and blocks publication when provenance is missing. Its defensibility is a transformation-survival corpus showing which marks remain detectable after resizing, transcoding, screenshotting and platform ingestion.
title: AI-Content Provenance Publish Gate
uncertainties: Whether CMS marketplaces permit a hard publish block
